requirement_en: Given pointers to two integers, swap their stored values in place.
Given pointers to two integers, set the first value to 0 only if the second value is nonzero, otherwise leave both unchanged.
Given pointers to three integers, reorder the values so they are in nondecreasing order.
Given pointers to two integers, return the larger of the two pointed values without modifying memory.
Given pointers to integers a and b, increase a by b and return the updated value of a.
Given unsigned x and nonzero unsigned y, store quotient and remainder of x divided by y through output pointers.
Given pointers to three integers, return the sum of the three pointed values.
Given pointers to two integers, return the sum of the two pointed values.
Given an integer array and its length, sort the array in nondecreasing order in place.
Given an integer array and its length, replace each element with double its original value.
Given an integer array and its length, reverse the element order in place.
Given an integer array and its length, set elements at even indices to 0 and leave odd indices unchanged.
Given two integer arrays and a length, return 1 if all compared elements are equal, otherwise return 0.
Given two integers, return the larger value.
Given an integer array, its length, and a constant c, add c to every array element in place.
Given an integer array and two valid indices, swap the elements at those indices.
Given a nonempty integer array and its length, return the maximum element.
Given an integer array, its length, and a target value, return the first index of the target or -1 if absent.
Given a nonnegative integer n, return the sum of all even numbers from 0 to n inclusive.
Given a nonnegative integer n, iterate a counter from 0 up to n and return n.
Given integers a and b with a nonnegative, return their product using repeated addition.
Given a nonnegative integer n, return n factorial.
Given a nonnegative integer n, return the sum of powers of two from 2^0 through 2^n.
Given a positive integer c, return c by counting loop iterations while decrementing from c to 0.
Given a nonnegative integer n, return the arithmetic sum of integers from 0 to n inclusive.
Run a loop that increments a counter from 0 until it reaches 30, yielding final value 30.
Given an integer array, target value, and length, return 1 if the target exists in the array, else 0.
Given an integer array, target value, and length, perform linear search and return 1 if found, otherwise 0.
Given nonnegative x and positive y, return the integer quotient of x divided by y using repeated subtraction.
Given an array, length, and value x, return the number of occurrences of x and output their total sum through a pointer.
Given a nonempty integer array and length, return the maximum array value.
Given an integer array and length, return 1 if every element is even, otherwise return 0.
Given a sorted integer array, target value, and length, return the target index via binary search or -1 if not found.
Given an integer array and length, return the sum of its elements.
Given integers x and y, adjust y by +10 and x by -5, then return their sum.
Given three side lengths, return 1 if they satisfy triangle inequality, else return 0.
Given three angles, return 1 if all are positive and sum to 180, otherwise return 0.
Given pointers to two integers, swap their values.
Given principal, time, and rate, return simple interest computed as p*n*r/100.
Given integer x and nonnegative exponent n, return x raised to the power n.
Given two integers, return the greater one (or either when equal).
Given two nonnegative integers, return their greatest common divisor.
Given integers x and y, return the difference x minus y.
Given integer n, return 1 plus the count of terms in the sequence 7,10,13,... that are less than or equal to n.
Given two integers, return their sum.
Given an integer, return its absolute value.
Given x, y, and an output pointer r with y positive, return quotient and store remainder such that x = quotient*y + remainder and remainder < y.
Given a nonnegative integer x, return x by decrementing a counter to zero and counting iterations.
Given a nonzero integer selector a, choose fixed values and return 10 divided by their sum (which evaluates to 1 for nonzero a).
Given a nonempty integer array and its length, return the maximum element.
Given base and height, return the integer area of a triangle computed as base*height/2.
Given pointers to two separate integers and two values, store the first value in the first location and the second value in the second location.
Given pointers to two separate integers, reorder the two stored values so the first is no greater than the second.
Given a pointer to an integer and inclusive bounds, clamp the stored value into the range.
Given a pointer to an integer and a delta, add the delta to the stored value without overflowing int.
Given separate destination and source integer pointers, copy the source value to the destination only when the source is positive.
Given two readable integer pointers and an output pointer, store the maximum of the two input values.
Given two input integers by pointer, store their minimum and maximum in separate output pointers.
Given nonnegative x and positive y, compute quotient and remainder through separate output pointers.
Given an integer that is not INT_MIN and an output pointer, store its absolute value.
Given a pointer to an integer and an upper bound, increment the stored value only if it is below the bound.
Given a Point pointer and two coordinates, set the point fields to those coordinates.
Given a Point pointer and deltas, translate the point without overflowing either coordinate.
Given a Counter pointer, reset its value to zero when it is negative and otherwise leave it unchanged.
Given a rectangle with nonnegative bounded dimensions, return width times height.
Given a point with nonnegative bounded coordinates, return x plus y.
Given a Point pointer, swap its x and y fields.
Given a Range pointer, swap its bounds when necessary so lo is no greater than hi.
Given separate Point pointers, copy the source point into the destination point.
Given a point with nonnegative coordinates and a nonnegative factor, scale both coordinates in place.
Given a Counter pointer, increment value only when it is below limit.
Given a nonempty readable integer array, return its first element.
Given an integer array, length, index, and value, store the value at that index and leave other elements unchanged.
Given an integer array and an index, set the indexed element to zero only when it is negative.
Given an integer array and a nonnegative length, set every element in the range to zero.
Given separate source and destination integer arrays and a nonnegative length, copy the source range into the destination range.
Given an integer array whose elements are below INT_MAX, increment every element by one.
Given a readable integer array and length, return 1 iff every element is zero, otherwise return 0.
Given a readable integer array and length, return the first index containing zero, or -1 when no zero exists.
Given an integer array with at least two elements, swap the first and last elements.
Given an integer array, length, prefix length, and value, fill exactly the prefix with that value.
Given separate arrays, copy only the first k elements from source to destination and leave the rest of destination unchanged.
Given a readable array of nonnegative integers whose sum fits in int, return the sum.
Given an integer array with at least three elements, reverse the first three elements.
Given two readable arrays and a separate output array, store the elementwise maximum for each position.
Given an integer array, replace every negative element with zero and leave nonnegative elements unchanged.
Given two integers whose sum is within int range, return their sum.
Given two ordered integers, return their nonnegative difference.
Given two integers, return the first one when it is nonzero and otherwise return the second one.
Given an integer, return 1 when it is even and 0 otherwise.
Given an integer and inclusive ordered bounds, return the value clamped into the range.
Given a character code, return 1 exactly when it is an ASCII digit.
Given an ASCII lowercase letter, return its uppercase letter; otherwise return the input unchanged.
Given a byte buffer, length, and byte value, set every byte in the range to that value.
Given separate byte buffers and a nonnegative length, copy source bytes into destination bytes.
Given a readable byte buffer and length, return 1 iff at least one byte is zero.
Given a byte buffer, replace every occurrence of one byte value with another byte value.
Given a readable character buffer of length n containing a null byte, return the index of the first null byte.
Given a readable byte buffer containing a zero byte, return the number of nonzero bytes before the first zero.
Given a writable character buffer and an in-bounds index, write a null terminator at that index and leave other positions unchanged.
